clue.text: Jam session?

parts.note: read not as musicians improvising but as the daily period when roads are jammed with commuter traffic

explanation.surface: A musician asks about an improvised gig with other players.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jam session' sounds like jazz; the question mark tells you to read 'jam' as a traffic jam.
explanation.definitionFit: The commuting peak is when traffic jams form, a time of congestion on the roads.

clue.text: Right in the open, or hiding?

parts.note: out means exposed, in the open, no longer concealed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is better to come out into the open or stay concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' looks like concealment, the opposite of 'in the open', but here it means a thrashing or heavy defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is slang for a crushing defeat, and a rout is an overwhelming defeat.

clue.text: Thus house required part of our capital

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A building needed in a district of the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a district in central London's West End, which is 'our capital' for a British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district is one area of the British capital city.

clue.text: For fooling around with heroin you need tolerance

parts.note: horse is a slang name for heroin
play is the slack or give in a mechanism, its tolerance

explanation.surface: Advice that anyone messing about with drugs needs a high tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' and 'with ... you need' are link words; HORSE is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough boisterous play is fooling around, larking about physically.

clue.text: Football team, say, heading off shortly to represent country

parts.note: United is a common football club name, Manchester United for example
to state is to say

indicators.note: the heading or first letter is taken off the word shortly

explanation.surface: A football team's spokesman is about to depart to represent his nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off shortly' gives just the S of 'shortly'; 'to represent' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The USA is a nation, the American country.

clue.text: Characters in Eastenders or The Archers?

definitions.meaning: people from Bow, a district of London's East End, are men of Bow
archers shoot with bows, so they are men with bows

explanation.surface: Asking which soap opera, EastEnders or The Archers, a figure belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders and The Archers are British soap operas on TV and radio; the clue uses them literally: East End residents from Bow, and archers.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers are men who shoot with longbows; residents of Bow in East London can also be called that.

clue.text: Old quarter, also known as home for many Japanese

parts.note: S, south, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: An old district, otherwise called something else, houses many Japanese residents.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Japanese city is where millions of people of Japan live.

clue.text: Wives, perhaps, going over familiar plans

indicators.note: the mates go over, that is surround, the familiar word

parts.note: wives are an example of mates, spouses
china is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, a familiar friend

explanation.surface: Wives look over some well-known plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang: china plate means mate, hence a familiar friend; 'going over' means wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to plot or scheme, as a verb.

clue.text: He's responsible for many bloomers in a growing business

definitions.text: He's responsible for many bloomers in a growing business

parts.words: He's responsible for many bloomers in a growing business
parts.note: bloomers sound like blunders or underwear, but here they are flowering plants raised in a plant-growing trade

explanation.surface: Someone in an expanding firm keeps making blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' suggests mistakes and 'growing business' an expanding company; both are literal horticulture.
explanation.definitionFit: This person raises plants for sale, so is responsible for flowers in a horticultural trade.

clue.text: Company he and I run provided cooked chicken

indicators.note: cooked means altered or falsified, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm's partners run a business supplying cooked chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked chicken' looks like food, but 'cooked' is the anagram signal and 'chicken' means cowardly; 'provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for cowardly, lacking bravery.

clue.text: Nerve shown by side that holds the cup

parts.note: sauce is cheek, impudence, nerve
R, right, is a side

explanation.surface: A team shows nerve in hanging on to the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The cup sounds like a sporting trophy held by a side, but it is a teacup.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dish placed under a teacup supports it.

clue.text: Prevention, of trouble after man's reported with stocking

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is replaced by one sounding like it

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts, so man is a piece
a shop keeping goods is stocking them

explanation.surface: A man is said to have been arrested for wearing hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking' suggests hosiery but means keeping in stock; the man is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping order between hostile groups is a way to stop conflict breaking out.

clue.text: Restoring one in even greater organisation

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
organisation means arranging anew, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bringing a single unit back into an even bigger company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' looks like a company but is the anagram signal: EVEN GREATER becomes REGENERATVE, with I put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regenerative renews or revives, bringing back to health.

clue.text: Succeeded, having both the speed and the skill to become high-flier

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies
pace is speed
craft is skill

explanation.surface: An ambitious person succeeded by having both pace and talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests an ambitious achiever but means a vessel flying in space.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that travels beyond the atmosphere flies very high indeed.

clue.text: Side's opener isn't out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cricket team's opening batsman has not been dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: an opener and 'out' suggest batting. 'Side' is old slang for airs and swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Side, as in putting on side, means affectation or airs, a showy claim to importance.

clue.text: In returning will I repeat risk?

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
In says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether repeating something on a return trip is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked the hidden-word indicator; 'In' is it. The letters LIREP inside 'will I repeat' are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is danger, a synonym of risk.

clue.text: Underground railway carrying a senior civil servant

parts.note: underground means clandestine, secret

explanation.surface: A Tube line carrying a top Whitehall official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests the London Tube but means secret. In Britain a Permanent Secretary heads a government department.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent secretary is the most senior official in a British government department.

clue.text: Splitting to form an unofficial union

definitions.text: Splitting to form an unofficial union

parts.words: Splitting to form an unofficial union
parts.note: splitting means running off, and the union is a marriage made without parental consent

explanation.surface: A breakaway group forming its own unrecognised trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests industrial relations; 'splitting' is slang for leaving and the union is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away secretly to marry is leaving home to make a marriage without approval.

clue.text: Boat they emptied in dock at Channel Island

parts.note: to dock is to cut short

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, leaving the outer pair

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A vessel they cleared out in a harbour on one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a harbour but means cut. The CUTTY SARK is a famous tea clipper preserved at Greenwich.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic clipper ship is a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Final development, rejecting stone in a ring

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the whole assembled piece is read in reverse
the stone goes inside the pair of letters

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: The last stage of a project, discarding a jewel set in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: GEM inside A and O gives AGEMO; 'rejecting' turns all of that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end, the ultimate stage of anything.

clue.text: Is journalist unable to cross one bar, supported on one side only?

parts.note: can't means unable to
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lever is a bar used to prise
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Asking whether a reporter is unable to get past a single pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' and 'to cross' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam fixed at only one end, like a balcony projecting from a wall, is held up from just one side.

clue.text: Steep inclines might be unsettling expedition leaders

indicators.note: leaders means the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Climbers warn that steep slopes could unnerve those heading an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective about the inclines, but it is a verb meaning soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak or saturate it, to permeate thoroughly.

clue.text: He has to go both ways

indicators.note: says the name reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A man who is obliged to travel in both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: a man's name that reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common German male name, so a man.

clue.text: Top part of bridge

definitions.meaning: ...- as a prefix means chief or principal, as in archbishop
a curved span supporting a bridge

explanation.surface: The highest section of a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved supporting span is one element of a bridge; the same word as adjective means principal or leading.

clue.text: One way to present arms

parts.note: present arms sounds like a military salute, but here the arms are human limbs held with hands on hips

explanation.surface: A drill instruction on how soldiers should present their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present arms' is a military command; here the arms are limbs, held with hands on hips and elbows out.
explanation.definitionFit: The posture with hands on hips and elbows turned outward is a way of holding one's limbs.

clue.text: Pilot produced by film-maker

definitions.meaning: a pilot steers or guides, as one who directs
the person who directs a film

explanation.surface: A trial episode made by a movie maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' suggests a trial TV episode, but means a guide; 'produced by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One who guides is a pilot, and the person in charge of shooting a film holds that title.

clue.text: Gypsy fiddle

definitions.meaning: an itinerant mender of pots, a traveller
to fiddle is to tamper or mess about with something

explanation.surface: A Romany violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' suggests a violin but is the verb meaning tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling mender was a name for a traveller, and to fiddle with something is to tamper with it.

clue.text: Potential flier had cracking time with it — he got repeatedly excited

definitions.text: Potential flier had cracking time with it

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word got is used twice

parts.note: the word got, taken as written, once before doubling

explanation.surface: An excited man repeatedly got to have a great time with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a potential flier is an unhatched chick, which uses this to crack open its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick has a small hard point on its beak for breaking out of its shell when hatching.
